Recognise genocide of '71
2017-02-16T00:00:00+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/city/recognise-genocide-1971-1361857

War crimes trial campaigner Ekattorer Ghatak Dalal Nirmul Committee yesterday renewed its demand that Bangladesh officially recognise the genocide of 1971 and call for international recognition for the crime committed by the Pakistani occupation forces.

The call came from a discussion the Nirmul Committee organised at the capital's Institute of Engineers, Bangladesh, marking the 94th birth anniversary of Prof Kabir Chowdhury.

On the occasion, Liberation War Museum trustee Mofidul Haque delivered a memorial lecture titled "Recognition of Bangladesh Genocide: At Home and Abroad".

Different quarters try to demean the war crime trial, but they never dare deny the genocide, he said. "It is high time the country brings recognition for the genocide."

The Committee president, Shahriar Kabir, said Armenia, Mexico and Guatemala recognised the genocides committed in the countries, and they also observed "genocide day".

Bangladesh needs a law, recognising the 1971 genocide, he added.

Speaking as chief guest, Commerce Minister Tofail Ahmed said March 25 could be declared "genocide day" and he would convey the demand to the prime minister.

Historian Prof Muntassir Mamoon said, “It is disgraceful that the country observes a day for hand washing, while it is yet to dedicate a day for the genocide victims.”

British social activist Julian Francis, who earned recognition by the Bangladesh government for his contribution to the Liberation War, said a concerted effort of non-resident Bangladeshis and eminent citizens living in the country was required to fulfil the demand.

Justice Golam Rabbani, Nirmul Committee member Meghna Guhathakurta, and American jurist William Sloan also spoke at the discussion.
